title: Valparaíso Rising
premise: In the port town of Valparaíso, 1911, Xanthe Nakamura — son of a Japanese pearl diver and a Chilean laundress, indentured since childhood to the Meridian Trading Company — has survived by being invisible, keeping the company's ledgers and its secrets. When the army requisitions the harbor and demands the ledger recording every indentured diver's debt and death, Xanthe discovers the book also holds proof that Meridian has been selling divers' salvage rights to a cartel that has already killed to protect them. Armed with the ledger and an unlikely found family — a disgraced army cartographer, a smuggler's widow, and the company owner's defiant daughter — Xanthe must move the evidence past three checkpoints before the company burns its records and its witnesses. He succeeds at devastating cost, trading his own name and freedom to save the others, and ends the novel years later, free at last, watching a new generation of divers surface without ledgers to bind them.
about_author: Ines Yarrow is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipping manifests from Pacific trade routes. Valparaíso Rising is her second novel, drawn from the marginalia she found in indenture ledgers — the names written small, in the corners, where no one was meant to read them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Names
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A routine day in the Meridian counting house: Xanthe copies debt figures, erases a dead diver's name at his supervisor's order, and swallows the familiar silence. He visits his mother's grave on the cliff road, where he notices army surveyors measuring the harbor. Emotional beat: the quiet dread of a man who has learned that noticing things is dangerous.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Soldiers occupy the counting house at dawn; a Captain Ibarra demands all company ledgers, including the master indenture book Xanthe keeps. His supervisor hands over a forged copy and privately orders Xanthe to hide the real one — not from conscience, but because it holds Meridian's leverage. Beat: fear sharpening into reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Error
chapters.summary: Elena Vasquez's POV. Elena, a disgraced army cartographer reassigned to Valparaíso as punishment, maps the new checkpoints and realizes the harbor's charts have been altered to hide a cartel's salvage routes. She needs someone who knows the old ledgers. Beat: her pride warring with the thrill of being useful again.

chapters.title: Debts Written in Water
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe retrieves the true ledger from its hiding place beneath the pearl-sorting floor and reads, for the first time, the full record: divers worked to death, salvage rights sold to the Cortázar cartel, his own father's name on the final page. Beat: grief transmuting into fury.

chapters.title: The Widow of Calle Serrano
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol Ferreyra, whose smuggler husband died in Meridian's service, runs the tavern where the soldiers drink. She agrees to hide Xanthe and the ledger, seeing in him the boy her husband once was. Beat: the first fragile stitching of a found family.

chapters.title: What the Daughter Knows
chapters.summary: Camila Meridian's POV. Camila, the owner's daughter, confronts Xanthe, having discovered her father's cartel dealings in his private correspondence. She offers her access to the company seals — and her testimony — if he'll let her come with him. Beat: betrayal of blood for the sake of what's right.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. Elena lays out the route: the customs house, the garrison gate, the naval pier. Each checkpoint requires different papers, different lies. She and Xanthe rehearse until his silences become a language she can read. Beat: trust forming between two people trained not to trust.

chapters.title: The First Gate
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The customs house crossing: Xanthe hides ledger pages inside a shipment of his mother's old diving weights, using his indenture papers as cover. A clerk who once mocked him waves him through — and Xanthe realizes the contempt that caged him has become his disguise. Beat: bitter triumph.

chapters.title: A Name in the Margins
chapters.summary: Camila's POV. Camila searches her father's study for the cartel contracts and finds a photograph of the divers, her father's handwriting circling Xanthe's father's face: 'expendable.' She burns nothing, keeps everything. Beat: the moment loyalty to family dies.

chapters.title: Ibarra's Offer
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Captain Ibarra, not the fool he seems, summons Xanthe and offers him freedom papers in exchange for the real ledger — Ibarra intends to use it to blackmail Meridian, not to free anyone. Xanthe stalls, promising an answer. Beat: the seduction of the easy exit.

chapters.title: The Tavern Burns
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Meridian's men torch the tavern searching for the ledger; Marisol saves the cellar cache but loses her home, and a young stableboy ally is badly hurt. The found family shelters together in the smugglers' tunnels beneath the cliffs. Beat: grief that hardens into resolve.

chapters.title: Tunnels the Divers Dug
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In the tunnels, old divers tell Xanthe stories of his father he never knew — a man who kept a hidden list of the dead. Xanthe understands the ledger was never just Meridian's weapon; it was meant to be testimony. Beat: inheritance reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Second Gate
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. The garrison gate: Elena uses her uniform and forged orders to move a crate of 'survey documents' — the ledger — through, but Ibarra is present and nearly inspects it. Camila creates a diversion that costs her a public scene with her father. Beat: the family's first true act of sacrifice.

chapters.title: What Silence Costs
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe confesses to Marisol that he considered Ibarra's offer. She tells him about her husband's last silence — the one that killed him. Xanthe decides the ledger goes to the naval magistrate, not to any man's pocket. Beat: choosing the hard right.

chapters.title: The Cartel Answers
chapters.summary: Camila's POV. Cortázar's enforcers arrive in force; Meridian senior, panicking, orders the counting house records burned in two days. Camila steals the burn order and races to the tunnels. Beat: the clock becomes a character.

chapters.title: The Third Gate
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The naval pier: Xanthe must pass himself off as a diver conscripted for salvage work, swimming the ledger out to a waiting magistrate's boat. The water is where his father died and where Xanthe has never felt he belonged. Beat: terror and homecoming at once.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, underwater and interior. The dive itself — cold, dark, the ledger sealed in oilcloth against his chest. He surfaces inside the pier's shadow as a patrol boat's lantern sweeps the water. Beat: the quietest, most visceral chapter; a man choosing to rise.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. The magistrate reads the names aloud on the pier as soldiers and townsfolk gather; Meridian and Cortázar's men are arrested, but Ibarra escapes with a copy of key pages. Beat: vindication shadowed by unfinished danger.

chapters.title: Ibarra's Last Bargain
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Ibarra corners Xanthe with the stolen pages and his freedom papers, demanding silence in exchange for escape before the cartel's remaining men find him. Xanthe refuses — and Marisol, Elena, and Camila arrive, having followed him. Beat: the found family standing between him and the old life.

chapters.title: What the Harbor Keeps
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The final confrontation at the cliff road: Ibarra, betrayed by the cartel he tried to bargain with, is taken by the magistrate's men; Meridian senior's fate is sealed by his own daughter's testimony. Beat: justice without triumphalism — the cost is counted honestly.

chapters.title: Indenture's End
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The magistrate nullifies the indentures; Xanthe is offered a position keeping the new, honest harbor records and refuses — he will not spend his life inside another ledger. He chooses instead to dive, freely, for the first time. Beat: liberation as self-authorship.

chapters.title: Valparaíso Rising
chapters.summary: Camila's POV, years later. The four — Xanthe, Elena, Marisol, Camila — gather on the cliff above a changed harbor where divers work under their own names. Xanthe surfaces from a free dive, laughing. Beat: belonging finally, fully, found — the story's themes resolved in sunlight and salt air.
